```{r setup, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
options(dplyr.summarise.inform=FALSE) 
library(readxl)
library(gridExtra)
library(knitr)
get_os <- function(){
  sysinf <- Sys.info()
  if (!is.null(sysinf)){
  os <- sysinf['sysname']
  if (os == 'Darwin')
    os <- "osx"
  } else { ## mystery machine
    os <- .Platform$OS.type
    if (grepl("^darwin", R.version$os))
      os <- "osx"
    if (grepl("linux-gnu", R.version$os))
      os <- "linux"
  }
  tolower(os)
}
```

Objective

> ... Is it possible for you to post the FULL internal and comparison data sets (all students, all majors) for the CPC data and internal for all students all majors in one report? 3. Does she mean all the topics and all the sample groups for CPC by "FULL internal and comparison data sets"?

So,

Let's try to address the requests. First, sort out the ideas. List combinations of factors. Hand draw outcomes. Then, for each case, make a mock up. Finally, share the results.

In the presentation, I used a flow of past - present via trends and snapshot. Beth wants something different. She wants a flow from aggregate to individual objectives. Moreover, she wants to incorporate the difference charts, but not yet clear how it can be incorporated consistently.

The main restriction here is that ACBSP spreadsheet is strictly linear in presentation. In order to narrate the multidimensional story in such a linear presentation, I need to have an additional dimension.

Also, difference charts does not need to be a cross-section, snapshot. It can show aggregation as a static picture.

Coding idea: Use html table in output. I have Beth's input already in the Excel, so import it as a data. Move them around as needed and output as a table, including the graphs. It'll be easy to move things around and export.

### Try out a table output
First, read (a copy of) the current Figure 4.2.
```{r}
fig42 <- read_excel(paste0(datapath, "Program Assessment\\fig42.xlsx"), "copy0809")
```

The `goal`, `tool`, and `result` columns are generated from the database spreadsheet. It's easy to purse them out. Use the type information to identify each row. Assessment used for multiple PLOs (e.g. ECO 3-5 external) can be identified with just one of the PLOs and later put back the label.
```{r}
fig42 <- fig42 %>% mutate(type = str_extract(tool, "Summative|Formative"),
                          ori = str_extract(tool, "External|Internal"),
                          plo = str_extract(id, "[A-Z]{3} \\d{1,2}"))
```

Now, try to produce a simple graph using the ID info.
```{r}
draw_time <- function(lo, ori = c("External", "Internal"),
                      typ = c("Summative", "Formative")){
  # Create a graph based on attributes
  # Data are drawn from `asm` data frame (previously computed values)
  ori <- match.arg(ori)
  typ <- match.arg(typ) 
  if (ori == "External"){
    outcome <- "external_outcome"
    target <- "external_target"
    ay <- "ay_external_n"
    tool <- asm_map %>% filter(plo == lo) %>%
      pull(external_tool_description)
    grp <- asm_map %>% filter(plo == lo) %>%
      pull(external_group)
    x <- asm %>% filter(plo == lo, type == typ)
    if (all(is.na(x$external_outcome))){
      return(NULL)}
  } else {
    outcome <- "internal_outcome"
    target <- "internal_target"
    ay <- "ay_internal_n"
    tool <- asm_map %>% filter(plo == lo) %>%
      pull(internal_tool_description)
    grp <- asm_map %>% filter(plo == lo) %>%
      pull(internal_group)
    x <- asm %>% filter(plo == lo, type == typ)
    if (all(is.na(x$internal_outcome))){
      return(NULL)}
  }
  ttl <- paste(lo, ori, typ)
  subt <- paste0("Tool: ", tool, "\nGroup: ", grp)
  p <- ggplot(x, aes_string(ay, outcome)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = 1), na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(size = 2, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_hline(aes_string(yintercept = target),
               alpha = 0.4, color = "red", na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent_format(accuracy = 5L))
  p <- p +
    labs(title = ttl, subtitle = subt) +
    xlab("Academic Year\nSample Size") +
    theme(plot.title = element_blank(),
          plot.subtitle = element_blank(),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "none") +
    ggthemes::theme_fivethirtyeight(base_size = 8)
  p
}
```

Then, make a table.
```{r outtable, fig.show="hide", eval=FALSE}
lres <- list()

x <- fig42[1, ]
lres[[1]] <- draw_time(x$plo, x$ori, x$type)
invisible(lapply(lres, print))

if (!interactive()) {
  out <- cbind(
    x[1, 1:6],
    table = sprintf("![](%s%s-%s.png)",
                    opts_current$get("fig.path"),
                    opts_current$get("label"),
                    1:length(lres))
    )
  kable(out)
}
```

Something I need in addition is the delta graph for external/internal. Wait, it's done that already. Get from presentation document.

```{r}
draw_delta <- function(prg, yr = 2019, ori = c("External", "Internal")){
  type <- match.arg(ori)
  
  if (ori == "External"){
    delta <- "ext_delta"
  } else {
    delta <- "int_delta"
  }
  
  title <- paste(prg, ori, "Deltas for", yr)
  subtitle <- "Differences between target achievements and actual outcomes"
  
  x <- asm %>% filter(program == prg, ay == yr)
  p <- ggplot(x, aes_string("plo", delta)) +
    geom_col(na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-0.2, 0.2), color = "red", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.0, color = "black", alpha = 0.4)
  p +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent_format(accuracy = 5L),
                       breaks = -5:5/10) +
    ggthemes::theme_fivethirtyeight(base_size = 8) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}
combine_deltas <- function(prg, yr = 2019){
  p1 <- draw_delta(prg, yr, "External")
  p2 <- draw_delta(prg, yr, "Internal")
  gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
}
p1 <- draw_delta("Business Core", 2019, "External")
p2 <- draw_delta("Business Core", 2019, "Internal")
```


```{r, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("fig/delta-bus-ext.png", p1, height = 2, width = 3.5, units = "in")
ggsave("fig/delta-bus-int.png", p2, height = 2, width = 3.5, units = "in")
```

```{r}
map_draw_time <- function(lo, ori = c("External", "Internal"),
                          typ = c("Summative", "Formative")){
  # Create a graph based on attributes
  # Data are drawn from `asm` data frame (previously computed values)
  ori <- match.arg(ori)
  typ <- match.arg(typ) 
  if (ori == "External"){
    outcome <- "external_outcome"
    target <- "external_target"
    ay <- "ay_external_n"
    tool <- asm_map %>% filter(plo == lo) %>%
      pull(external_tool_description)
    grp <- asm_map %>% filter(plo == lo) %>%
      pull(external_group)
    x <- asm %>% filter(plo == lo, type == typ)
    if (all(is.na(x$external_outcome))){
      return(NULL)}
  } else {
    outcome <- "internal_outcome"
    target <- "internal_target"
    ay <- "ay_internal_n"
    tool <- asm_map %>% filter(plo == lo) %>%
      pull(internal_tool_description)
    grp <- asm_map %>% filter(plo == lo) %>%
      pull(internal_group)
    x <- asm %>% filter(plo == lo, type == typ)
    if (all(is.na(x$internal_outcome))){
      return(NULL)}
  }
  ttl <- paste(lo, ori, typ)
  subt <- paste0("Tool: ", tool, "\nGroup: ", grp)
  
  draw_time(x, ay, outcome, ttl, subt)
}
map_draw_time("ACC 1", "External", "Summative")
```
